upstream.inspection: tagged source read through primary web sources; not a byte/build attestation of the deployed server

primary_sources.facts: BACKUP_ADMIN is required; concurrent backup holders are allowed; session termination releases its lock. Ordinary DML remains possible; temporary-table DDL and binary-log creation are exceptions. Account-management operations are blocked. These documented categories do not replace targeted deployed-server tests.

The SQL command requests the backup lock with nontransactional duration. The implementation uses BACKUP_LOCK/SHARED/MDL_EXPLICIT; DDL uses the incompatible intention-exclusive mode. Explicit release removes backup-lock tickets.
lock_object_name handles function, procedure and event namespaces and requests an intention-exclusive BACKUP_LOCK along with object/schema locks.

Routine create, drop and alteration enter lock_object_name. This supplies a source-level reason to test backup-lock coverage of routines instead of assuming they escape because they lack individual files.

Strong table-DDL name-lock acquisition adds intention-exclusive BACKUP_LOCK. Temporary-table and LOCK TABLES paths have explicit conditions; coverage cannot be inferred merely from the spelling of a statement.
View creation/alteration opens its table list through the table-open machinery. The entire call path and deployed waiting behavior remain an acceptance requirement.
metadata_locks exposes BACKUP LOCK, SHARED, EXPLICIT, GRANTED/PENDING and OWNER_THREAD_ID. Instrumentation and exact thread mapping must be proved; a timeout alone is not lock evidence.

current_code_findings: Collect calls SQLRegistry.begin; this begins via DB.BeginTx and exposes only Tx.
The only collector commit is tx.Commit; the policy interface has Early/Lock/Recheck and no post-commit session-release owner.
The current worker grants validator permits global REFERENCES, not BACKUP_ADMIN. The observer's exact profile also does not approve BACKUP_ADMIN.
No backup lock is currently acquired; this is a prospective integration hazard, not evidence of an existing leaked production lock.
Go Tx completion releases its connection capability; Tx cannot issue a later unlock. Conn.Close is pool return, not proof of physical disconnect.
The cached mysql v1.9.0 ResetSession checks liveness/busy state; it does not issue a server reset or unlock. Pool reset must not be treated as cleanup.
rejected_shortcuts: acquire LOCK INSTANCE in Early and rely on transaction Commit/Rollback for unlock
unlock before commit to make a Tx-only API convenient
after commit run UNLOCK INSTANCE through DB.Exec and assume the pool gives back the old session
rely on Conn.Close or driver ResetSession to physically disconnect/reset a locked session
let a separate lock-owner connection die between a last recheck and collector commit
treat BACKUP_ADMIN as already approved, or use root/disable the exact grants gate
treat the Go fake-driver experiment as MySQL DDL blocking or rollback proof
candidate_constraints: A reviewed collector owner must retain one exact physical SQL connection through freeze acquisition, RR work, the sole commit/rollback and cleanup.

Acquire freeze before metadata observation and protect through commit; do not release to satisfy a Tx-only API. Placement relative to current worker admission and existing lock prefixes needs explicit review.
Preserve the original peer, worker, grant, schema, source, scope, retention, reservation and group rollback guards. No freeze substitutes for any of them.

Known transaction completion is followed by explicit unlock on that same connection before any allowed pool return. Unknown commit, failed cleanup or cancellation requires verified discard handling and a distinct truthful outcome.
Physical discard must use the database/sql bad-connection contract or a separately verified equivalent; ordinary Conn.Close is insufficient. Never leak raw driver handles.
Cleanup may not issue unlock against a fresh unrelated pooled connection, create a permissive worker profile or claim rollback after an ambiguous commit.

Review session initialization and pool exclusivity: temporary tables can survive pooling and are not frozen. Also review restoration or discard of session settings such as lock_wait_timeout and time zone.
BACKUP_ADMIN is a new global capability for the candidate worker profile. Account/grants approval, global DDL disruption bounds and recovery procedures remain unapproved.
Maintain bounded original authorization context, bounded wait and cleanup behavior; stop batches on unresolved commit/cleanup outcomes without claiming a known rollback.
Actual program observation, approved expected digests and complete catalog/import/logical/bootstrap/reference policy remain separately required.

canary DML rolls back; original group/tombstone/capacity remains one atomic transaction; BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK do not silently release the session freeze
create/alter/drop/rename and new cross-schema incoming FK wait on the exact holder BACKUP LOCK, then resolve after its release
procedure/function create, alter and drop with exact connection/thread/lock evidence
trigger create/drop, event create/alter/drop and view create/alter/drop/algorithm change with actual lock evidence
account/grant/revoke operations and their lock ordering; unrelated legal DML remains possible and no authority check is bypassed
holder connection killed before/during writes rolls back; cancellation and lost commit response preserve truthful outcome and remove or surface the exact held lock
after known unlock the next borrower sees no old lock; ambiguous/failed cleanup uses a new physical session, never a locked pool return
prove this owner's lock rather than treating another holder's lock as its own or as its cleanup failure
dedicated clean-session/pool protocol excludes stale temporary-table shadowing and stale session settings; documented temporary-DDL exceptions are not hidden
actual bounded acquisition, full metadata capture, global DDL disruption and cross-participant deadlock behavior
one real Collect with original references/owner/capacity/deadline/nonce/audits and late-failure rollback through actual freeze protocol
